test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 29 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

The shopkeeper must have misguided the customers to purchase the faulty watches.

options.text: The customers must be misguided by the shopkeeper to purchase the faulty watches.
The customers must have been misguided by the shopkeeper to purchase the faulty watches.
The customers must have been misguided by the shopkeeper to have purchased the faulty watches.
The customers must have been misguided by the shopkeeper to be purchasing the faulty watches.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The shopkeeper must have misguided the customers to purchase the faulty watches."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the customers" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "must have misguided" to "must have been misguided" (modal perfect passive).
 
• Ensure the rest of the sentence retains its original meaning, including "to purchase the faulty watches."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The customers must have been misguided by the shopkeeper to purchase the faulty watches."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The customers must be misguided by the shopkeeper to purchase the faulty watches." – Incorrect tense (present modal passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"The customers must have been misguided by the shopkeeper to have purchased the faulty watches." – Incorrect meaning and usage of "to have purchased."
 
• **Option 4: **"The customers must have been misguided by the shopkeeper to be purchasing the faulty watches." – Incorrect use of "to be purchasing."
